To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel dual doping strategy to manipulate the dehydrogenation process, which enables a bifunctional Co3N nanorod catalyst with excellent catalytic performance towards HzOR (55 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm-2) and HER (41 mV at a similar current density).
we have demonstrated a highly active Co3N based bifunctional catalyst for both HzOR and HER, which is capable to drive a self powered H 2 production system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bifunctional catalyst for hydrazine assisted H2 production.
the design of bifunctional electrocatalysts for the direct oxidation of hydrazine to produce hydrogen.
the design of bifunctional P/W co doped Co 3 N nanowire array as a highly efficient catalyst for both hydrazin oxidation reaction (Hzor) and hydrogen evolution (Her) reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bifunctional P/W co doped Co 3N electrode with excellent catalytic performance towards both HzOR and HER is a promising alternative for self powered H2 generation.
the dual doping strategy can significantly improve the catalytic kinetics of the dehydrogenation process and thus enable the highly efficient hydazine oxidation assisting self-powered H2 production.
a dual doping strategy is developed for Co3N to enable highly efficient hydazone oxidation assisting self powered hydrogen production.

we report a bifuctional Co3N nanomaterial that can catalyze both hydrazie oxidation and hydrogen evolution reaction with high catalytic activity.

we report a bifuctional P, W doped Co3 nanowires electrode for both hydrazin oxidation reaction (Hzor) and hydrogen evolution reactions (her), and achieve a low cell voltage of only 28mV to drive 10mAcm 2 in two-electrode system.
we developed a dual doped Co3 N nanowires electrode with remarkable bifunctionality toward hydrazine and H 2 catalysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bifunctional catalyst could enable self powered hydrazine electrolysis, which is a new strategy for H2 production.
a dual doped Co3Nx catalyst with high catalytic performance for both hydrazin oxidation and hydrogen evolution can be obtained by a simple doping method.

the bifunctional catalyst could enable a self powered H 2 production system by directly integrating the hydrazine electrolyzer and direct fuel cell, which may be of great interest to the renewable H2 production and storage.
